answer: Because the ember measurement is attested to the cipher verifier, the whisper audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. A farm needs 2 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. Each copy needs 4 hours of work. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
